articles.title: Judi Dench has inspired a new decorating trend – and I oppose it with every fibre of my being
articles.summary: Reverse decluttering is here, prompting a shudder from me and my fellow neat freaks. Why would you want to be surrounded by mementos when you could be perfectly tidy? Older doesn’t always mean wiser. Jo Whiley has spoken about a home hack she picked up from – clang!
body: Whiley went to interview Dench for her RHS Roots podcast and found the actor’s house “packed with family photographs, children’s drawings and memories everywhere”. Mind-blowingly, she means this as a positive. “Seeing Judi’s reminded me that lived-in spaces are often the most beautiful because they reflect a lifetime of love, family and shared experiences,” she says. “I suddenly thought: ‘Why am I putting all these things away?’” As soon as I got home, I immediately put all the family photographs back out.” TLDR: I cleaned up and then I made it all messy again. Shudder.

He has a mustard cravat that also smells like mustard, despite many spins in the washing machine, which belonged to a great-great-aunt’s husband’s brother. You’d be amazed how few occasions call for a cravat, unless you assumed it was none at all. My husband is like a bird refusing to budge from its nest because it’s fiercely protecting eggs, but instead of eggs it’s nonfunctional laptops, antique T-shirts and a pungent cravat.
points: Reverse decluttering is here, prompting a shudder from me and my fellow neat freaks.
Why would you want to be surrounded by mementos when you could be perfectly tidy?

articles.title: Swimmers warned of toxic algae at newly designated Thames bathing site
articles.summary: People told they and their pets should keep out of river at Ham amid anger over Thames Water’s treated sewage plan. Swimmers are being warned not to enter the water at the first official bathing site on the River Thames, in south-west London, because of toxic blue-green algae in the water.
body: The blue-green algal blooms are rare in moving water but are likely to be caused by the extreme heat, low river flow, and nutrient pollution from sewage waste.
Thames Water’s Hogsmill sewage treatment plant, in Kingston upon Thames, is situated three miles upstream of the Ham bathing site.

Marlene Lawrence, of the swimming group Teddington Bluetits, which successfully applied for the bathing water designation at Ham, said: “This is so unusual to get blue-green algae in a moving body of water. It is the first time in nearly six years of swimming here that this has happened.
“The river is very low-flowing at the moment because of the lack of rain and the high temperatures we are having. With climate change, this is likely to happen more.”

articles.title: Matthew Higham obituary
articles.summary: My former partner and friend Matthew Higham, who has died aged 79, lived a cheerfully chequered life: running away from London to Scotland as a teenager to marry his pregnant first wife, Kay, when their parents forbade it; training as a blacksmith and at the E15 theatre school in London, alongside…
body: Having driven trucks to various parts of the world, in 1978 he co-founded, with his brother Ben, St Giles European Transport, a specialist antiques haulage company in Norwich, and afterwards became an antiques dealer in the city.

Restless by nature, Matthew’s antique hunting gave him licence to roam across Europe, and later the US and China, finding worn and weathered treasures in remote places. Along the way he collected many experiences and stories, which he recounted with delight to anyone who would listen. Over the years he also accumulated two wives, two partners and five children.

Born in Holborn, central London, to David, a literary agent, and Helen (nee Witton), a journalist, Matthew grew up in Hampstead, north London. He attended various schools in the area, but none of them recognised his dyslexia, and he survived by becoming the class entertainer. Largely self-educated, in his teens he became politically aware, joined at least one Aldermaston march, and left the Sea Scouts to briefly hook up with the Communist Party of Great Britain.

articles.title: Why Anthony Bourdain’s Editor Wanted ‘Tony’ to Be Darker
articles.summary: There are two types of biopics: those that unconventionally show, and those that exhaustively tell. Thank goodness that Tony, the highly anticipated A24 biopic about the late Anthony Bourdain, takes the former route.
body: Eater spoke with the film’s screenwriters about casting the titular role, chef cameos, and more BTS moments.

Then again, successfully pitching a Bourdain biopic to his estate was always going to be a big swing. I spoke with Todd Bartels and Lou Howe about what made that swing possible (for one: bringing on Kimberly Witherspoon, Bourdain’s literary agent and friend, as an executive producer); which cast member demonstrated the best culinary chops; and who they could imagine playing an older, more seasoned Anthony Bourdain.
Eater: How did you strike the balance between making a movie for the passionate Anthony Bourdain fans, and viewers who may know very little about him?

Lou Howe: I was anxious about that [ laughs ], especially at the very beginning. But [we] just [tried] to make a good movie, and hope that the entertainment factor and emotional engagement hits the target well enough. We started this whole process as fans, so in that way we felt relatively comfortable servicing fellow fans. You want to write a good story that people can plug into no matter who the character is. Of course, there are some Kitchen Confidential Easter eggs.
points: There are two types of biopics: those that unconventionally show, and those that exhaustively tell.
Thank goodness that Tony, the highly anticipated A24 biopic about the late Anthony Bourdain, takes the former route.

articles.title: What to Know About Angie Nixon, the Progressive Lawmaker Who Swept Florida’s U.S. Senate Primary
articles.summary: Florida’s U.S. Senate primary ended in an upset when progressive candidate Angie Nixon triumphed over her more moderate opponent, Alex Vindman, to win the Democratic nomination for the Senate.
body: Nixon, who is also a member of the Working Families Party and the Democratic Socialists of America, is the latest left-wing, progressive candidate to prevail against moderate, establishment Democrats. Earlier this month, Abdul El-Sayed earned the Democratic nomination in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race against both incumbent Mallory McMorrow and Haley Stevens, a more moderate candidate. And last year, New York City elected Zohran Mamdani mayor over former New York governor Andrew Cuomo, whose own Democratic primary loss spurred him to run as an Independent in the general election.

While the democratic socialist label remains charged, Nixon is adamant that she does not want to be defined by the party she belongs to (she joined the DSA at the end of July). “[W]e showed the world what people of Florida are all about,” Nixon said in an address to her supporters yesterday. “Medicare for all. Universal child care. Real, affordable housing. Fully funded public education. And an end to senseless wars.”
Below, here’s what you should know about Florida’s Democratic nominee for the United States Senate, Angie Nixon.

articles.title: 15 Best Anti-Aging Serums For Smoother, Plumper Skin at Any Age
articles.summary: In choosing the best anti-aging serums, experts recommend incorporating not only SPF, but ingredients like retinol, peptides, and vitamin C. Shop our favorites here.
body: Before my internal monologue spun out too far, I asked Carol Eisenstat, MD, a board-certified physician specializing in facial aesthetics, how the pros pick a lane. “The best serum is the one you’ll use daily, and that has data behind it,” she said. “When recommending a skin-care product to patients, I look for formulations that have clinical data published on them, incorporate ingredients that have a mechanism of action that makes sense, and also fit into my patients’ daily routines. The serum doesn’t have to be the most expensive or the most trendy.”

That said, some trending skin-care ingredients —including growth factor technology and exosomes—have impressed Dr. Eisenstat for how well they improve texture, firmness, and speed healing after in-office procedures. At the same time, classic anti-aging ingredients like retinoids and gentle AHAs still have a place in a modern regimen, and K-beauty serums —focused less on correction and more on barrier support—are increasingly in demand. Which formulas are the best from each category? Ahead, find the top dermatologist-approved serums for brightening, hydrating, exfoliating, and tackling other signs of aging.

articles.title: Björk, an Eclipse, and 40 Years of Icelandic Underground Music
articles.summary: Björk’s eclipse rave was more than a party: It was a celebration of the Icelandic label and creative community that helped shape the country’s singular music scene.
body: I was warned that the light change right before totality would feel the strangest. As I looked up at the cloud-strewn Icelandic sky, the crowd pulsing around me, it was as if the world had transformed into a film noir—our upturned faces suddenly cast in washed-out shades of grey.
Then, for a minute, everything slipped into pitch-black darkness. In those few moments, strangers hugged; I cried and laughed simultaneously; and one person yelled “You’re doing great, moon!”
When the moon crossed between the Earth and the sun on August 12, we couldn’t see the total solar eclipse —but we could feel it. We were standing in the moon’s shadow.

There were no groans, complaints, or frowns, in part because our anticipation was two-fold. The dark green weather forecast (indicating the heaviest level of cloud coverage) had sent many of the more devoted eclipse chasers north, chasing clear skies. But thousands of us chose to remain in Víðistaðatún, a sculpture park strewn with massive lava rocks in Hafnarfjörður about six miles from Downtown Reykjavik, for Echolalia, a one-day rave headlined by Björk, arguably Iceland’s most famous musician.

articles.title: I Finally Tried A313, France’s Cult-Favorite Retinoid
articles.summary: A313 is one of the most popular French pharmacy products, but does it actually live up to the hype? Here, Vogue explores the retinoid’s popularity and gets the inside scoop on its benefits.
body: Rarely do I succumb to a TikTok beauty product recommendation. But the A313 Vitamin A pomade has been in my orbit long before social media claimed it; for years many of my US editor friends and go-to beauty experts have raved about its effects on skin. So now that my algorithm is being fed an endless amount of French pharmacy hauls, I finally made it a goal to brave the Paris summer crowds at the Pharmacie Citypharma on 26 Rue du Four to buy my first tube.

To my surprise, the French don’t actually consider A313 an anti-aging skincare product. As Natacha Bonjout, French pharmacist and founder of Bonjout Beauty, explains, it has been used for decades as more of a functional medicine. “The reality is more nuanced,” Bonjout says. “The product is old, but the story around it is new.”

But thanks to America’s fascination with French pharmacy culture, the product has gotten a new life thanks to social media. Whether intended or not, it has become the skin-care symbol of French beauty. “It feels like an insider secret,” she goes on to say. “So I don’t think [US] consumers are only buying A313; they’re buying into the idea of French pharmacy.”
points: A313 is one of the most popular French pharmacy products, but does it actually live up to the hype?
